Ann Radcliffe, The Mysteries of Udolpho.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/ann-radcliffe/the-mysteries-of-udolpho

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Ann Radcliffe, the author, died 1823.

First publication of the text used: 1794, in London, England (SE colophon: 'The Mysteries of Udolpho was published in 1794 by Ann Radcliffe'; Wikipedia, 'The Mysteries of Udolpho': it 'appeared in four volumes on 8 May 1794 from G. G. and J. Robinson of London').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1794, long before 1931, so it is in the United States public domain. The edition's own statement of rights says the same.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom, first publication in London): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die did so in 1823, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1894.

The edition's own statement of rights:
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: published in 1794 by Ann Radcliffe; no translator or editor named
- Wikipedia, 'The Mysteries of Udolpho': first appeared on 8 May 1794 from G. G. and J. Robinson of London
- Wikidata Q231944 (Ann Radcliffe), death 1823-02-07, as recorded in the facts file
